title: Photoworks notifies customers of e-commerce attack exposing names, emails and some card data and passwords
date_note: Day Photoworks' notice was reported to the California Attorney General (Reported Date 11/17/2026 on the Attorney General's breach list); the sample letter itself is dated only "November __, 2026". The notice says the attack started on or about September 1, 2026 and was discovered on October 22, 2026.
place: United States (headquarters not stated in the notice)
geo_basis: country only; the notice gives no company address (it says the attack was reported to the San Francisco Police Department)
summary: Photoworks says in a breach notice filed with California's Attorney General that a sophisticated attack on its e-commerce system started on or about September 1, 2026, was discovered on October 22 and fully contained on October 28. Its investigation found customer names, addresses and emails compromised and, for a limited set of individuals, credit card information and/or website passwords. Photoworks reported it to the San Francisco Police Department and the FBI.
plain: Photoworks says an attack on its online shop began about September 1 and was found on October 22; it exposed customer names, addresses and emails, and for some people card details or passwords.
exec: E-commerce compromise exposed customer contact data and, for some, credit card information and website passwords.
action: Photoworks' notice says affected customers who have not logged in since November 6, 2026 must reset their password, should change it on other sites where it is reused, and should monitor financial accounts.
impact: Customer names, addresses and emails; credit card information and/or passwords for a limited set of individuals. No number of people given.

sources.name: California Attorney General breach register entry: Photoworks Inc.
Photoworks breach notification letter (sample filed with the California Attorney General)

key_findings: Attack on the e-commerce system started on or about September 1, 2026; discovered October 22 and fully contained October 28, 2026
Customer names, addresses and emails compromised; for a limited set of individuals, credit card information and/or website passwords
Reported to the San Francisco Police Department and the FBI
recommendations: Reset the Photoworks password unless logged in on or after November 6, 2026, and change it on other sites where reused
Monitor financial accounts and contact the bank about unauthorized activity

validation.note: Primary source: Photoworks' own notice letter filed with the California Attorney General (register entry read; Reported Date 11/17/2026 from the Attorney General's breach list). No news coverage read.

evidence.quote: We write to advise you of a sophisticated attack on Photoworks’ e-commerce system that started on or about September 1, 2026.
The attack was discovered on October 22, 2026, was fully contained on October 28, 2026 and has been reported to the San Francisco Police Department and the FBI.
Unless you have logged onto the website on or after November 6, 2026, you will need to reset your password.

review.note: unsourced consequence: exec said card-not-present fraud and password reuse risk, which the letter does not state; now restates the letter. Title, dates (AG list 11/17/2026), contained 28 Oct, data types and action checked against the letter.
